summary: Patrick R. Uhlmann is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued his doctoral studies at the University of California, Los Angeles, where he was attested as a PhD candidate in 2012, studying under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Patrick de Silva Kularatne (1893–1976) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at University College London and the University of London around 1913 to 1918, later serving as Principal of Ananda College from circa 1918 to 1943.

Patrul Rinpoche (1808–1887) was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar and teacher. He studied under numerous masters, including Jigme Gyelwai Nyugu from around 1830 to 1842 and Zhabkar Tsokdruk Rangdrol, and taught prominent figures such as Shenphen Nangwa and Terton Sogyal.

Paul B. Courtright is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He served as a colleague at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and held positions at Emory University, where he was attested in 1998 and as Professor Emeritus in 2026.

Paul B. Donnelly is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who holds a post at Northern Arizona University. He studied under doctoral supervisor Geshe Lhundub Sopa, attested in 1997, as well as traditional teachers including Yeshe Thapkay.

Paul Bernard (1929–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure and University of Paris 1 Pantheon-Sorbonne, he directed the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan (1965–1980) and taught at EPHE (1981).

Paul Carus (1852–1919) was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Hermann Günther Grassmann, earned his PhD at the University of Tübingen (~1875–1876), and worked at the Open Court Publishing Company (~1887–1919).

Paul Copp is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies who earned his PhD from Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser. He held posts at Western Michigan University and the University of Chicago, attested as Associate Professor in 2026.

Paul Crowe is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He pursued graduate studies at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura and Daniel L. Overmyer, and served as a professor at Simon Fraser University, attested in 2010.

Paul David Devanandan (1901–1962) was a religious studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Nizam College, Presidency College, and Yale University, he taught philosophy and religions at United Theological College, Bangalore (1932–1949), and directed CISRS beginning in 1956.

Paul David Numrich is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Michigan in 1992. In 2006, he was attested at Loyola University Chicago and the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus.

Paul Debes (1906–2004) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He founded the Buddhistisches Seminar (1948), the Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg (1954), where he was a board member, and the Deutsche Buddhistische Gesellschaft (1955), and taught Hellmuth Hecker.

Paul Demiéville (1894–1979) was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Édouard Chavannes. He held the Chair of Chinese Language and Literature at the Collège de France (1946–1964) and taught at EPHE and INALCO.

Paul Deussen (1845–1919) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Christian Lassen and completed his Habilitation at Humboldt University of Berlin, where he served as Privatdocent (1881–1887) before becoming a professor at Kiel University in 1889.

Paul Dundas (1952–2023) was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He led Asian studies at the University of Edinburgh (~1976–2017) and served as head of the Pali Text Society (~1993–2023).

Paul Ekman (1934–2025) studied at New York University (~1952–1954) and Adelphi University (~1954–1958). He served on the faculty at the University of California, San Francisco from circa 1960 to 2004.

Paul F. Knitter (1939–) is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University (~1958–1966) and the University of Marburg (~1969–1972), and later held a post at Union Theological Seminary (~2007–2017).

Paul Fredericq (1850–1920) was a history and archaeology scholar who completed his doctorate at the University of Liège (~1871–1875). He served as a professor at the University of Liège (~1879–1883) and Ghent University, where he became rector in 1919.

Paul Fuller is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Paul Dundas and completed his PhD at the University of Bristol under Rupert Gethin. As of 2026, he is attested at the University of Edinburgh.

Paul G. Hackett is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as South Asia Bibliographer and Tibetan Collection curator at the University of Virginia (attested 1994, 2003) and later held research and lecturing posts at Columbia University (attested 2003–2016).
